Fertility rates from the birth history

Source: R/rates.R
bdhs_fertility.Rd

Computes the total fertility rate (TFR), age-specific fertility rates (ASFR) or the general fertility rate (GFR) with the DHS method: births in the reference period are classified by the mother's age at birth, and woman-years of exposure in each five-year age group are counted month by month within the period. Because every BDHS interviewed only ever-married women, exposure is multiplied by the all-woman factor (awfact/100) so that the rates refer to all women.

Usage

bdhs_fertility(
  data,
  type = c("tfr", "asfr", "gfr"),
  period = 36,
  by = NULL,
  se = TRUE,
  awfact = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  survey = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A women's recode (IR) data frame with the birth history in wide form (b3_01, b3_02, ...), the interview date v008, the woman's date of birth v011, the weight v005, the cluster v021 and the all-woman factors (awfactt, ...).

type

One of "tfr" (births per woman), "asfr" (births per 1,000 women, by age group) or "gfr" (births per 1,000 women age 15-44).

period

Length of the reference period in months before the interview (DHS standard: 36 for TFR/ASFR/GFR). The month of the interview is excluded.

by

Optional character vector of grouping variables (woman-level).

se

If TRUE (default), compute jackknife standard errors and confidence intervals.

awfact

All-woman factor. NULL (default) chooses it from by (awfactu for v025, awfactr for v024, awfacte for v106, awfactw for v190, otherwise awfactt); FALSE disables the adjustment (for all-woman samples); a column name uses that column.

level

Confidence level.

survey

Optional survey reference, overriding detection.

Value

A tibble with columns survey_id, the by variables, indicator, age_group, estimate, se, ci_low, ci_high, n_births (unweighted births in the period), exposure (weighted woman-years), n_women, n_psu and period.

Details

Standard errors use the DHS jackknife: each primary sampling unit is deleted in turn and the rate recomputed, giving \(SE = \sqrt{(k-1)/k \sum (r_{(j)} - r)^2}\) for \(k\) clusters.

See also

bdhs_mortality(), bdhs_estimate()

Examples

ir <- bdhs_simulate(2017, "IR")
bdhs_fertility(ir)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 12
#>   survey_id indicator age_group estimate    se ci_low ci_high n_births exposure
#>   <chr>     <chr>     <chr>        <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 BD2017DHS tfr       15-49         2.71 0.179   2.36    3.06      167    1928.
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: n_women <int>, n_psu <int>, period <int>
bdhs_fertility(ir, "asfr", se = FALSE)
#> # A tibble: 7 × 12
#>   survey_id indicator age_group estimate    se ci_low ci_high n_births exposure
#>   <chr>     <chr>     <chr>        <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 BD2017DHS asfr      15-19         95.1    NA     NA      NA      167    1928.
#> 2 BD2017DHS asfr      20-24        215.     NA     NA      NA      167    1928.
#> 3 BD2017DHS asfr      25-29        105.     NA     NA      NA      167    1928.
#> 4 BD2017DHS asfr      30-34         71.5    NA     NA      NA      167    1928.
#> 5 BD2017DHS asfr      35-39         27.6    NA     NA      NA      167    1928.
#> 6 BD2017DHS asfr      40-44         26.8    NA     NA      NA      167    1928.
#> 7 BD2017DHS asfr      45-49          0      NA     NA      NA      167    1928.
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: n_women <int>, n_psu <int>, period <int>
bdhs_fertility(ir, "tfr", by = "v025", se = FALSE)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 13
#>   survey_id v025  indicator age_group estimate    se ci_low ci_high n_births
#>   <chr>     <fct> <chr>     <chr>        <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 BD2017DHS urban tfr       15-49         2.63    NA     NA      NA       81
#> 2 BD2017DHS rural tfr       15-49         2.85    NA     NA      NA       86
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: exposure <dbl>, n_women <int>, n_psu <int>, period <int>
